notes: The ten national values, who each polity is at war with, and its war weariness.
Everything is zero except where a war is running at the start date.
WAR WEARINESS, from plans.md, Armies movement and occupation:
baseWeariness = min(3, daysAtWar / 720) + 400 * cumulativeDeaths / population
times wearinessModifier
per battle      weariness += baseWeariness * (100 * deaths / population) * ground
ground 1.0 on ground the country owns, 2.5 on ground it does not
The calendar half stops at 3, so a long quiet war stays cheap. Deaths are a
share of the country s own population, so 200,000 dead is not the same thing
to a kingdom and to an empire.
wearinessModifier is where national spirits, policies and ministers will land:
Propaganda -25%, Censor the press -25%, Secret police -20%, War bonds -15%,
the Security minister -10% to -20% by trait, Rationing +20%. Multiply them.
THE CONTINENTAL REVOLUTION, 25 Mithalvan 1923 to the start date, 1,232 days.
Ends at the Treaty of Saint Tofos on 2 Mithalbruni 1926, 22 days into play, so
the two sides are in ceasefire and negotiating. Simulated month by month.
CNC  Continental Confederation
population 5,295,000, dead 85,000, which is 1.61% of it
wearinessModifier 0.75  -- a revolution with a cause, read as Propaganda
ground rising 1.0 to 2.5 across the war as it advanced out of Latoma
-> baseWeariness 6.1, weariness 10.1
SVP  Protectorate of Sanatese Vortopaga
population 15,348,000, dead 250,000, which is 1.63% of it
wearinessModifier 1.00  -- a colonial administration with nothing to offer
ground 1.0 throughout, defending its own
-> baseWeariness 8.2, weariness 6.9
The two lost near-identical shares of their people and the CC s base still
comes out lower. That gap is the modifier and nothing else, which is the point
of holding the modifier separately. The CC s total weariness is nonetheless the
higher of the two, because it spent the war on ground it did not own.
THE CUNARIAN CIVIL WAR, 7 Ungervan 1923, 916 days, three-way, still running.
All three factions claim the whole of each other s ground, so all three fight
at ground 1.0: a civil war is fought at home by everyone in it.
CANON TOLL: 300,000 military and 450,000 civilian across the whole war,
1923 to 1934. At the start date 916 of about 4,042 days have run, 22.7% of it,
taken as 25% for the heavy opening: 75,000 military and 112,500 civilian dead
so far. Military split by population share; civilians weighted toward the
Franzonist government, being fought by two sides at once.
deaths counts civilians as well as soldiers, at ground 1.0.
Their weariness is STACKED on the Second Sapient War. Cunaria led the Triple
Alliance with Twadamia and Aroyan from 4 Sithvan 1912 and fought 2,224 days,
until the Caitponte Revolution of 20 Sithvan to 8 Ungertre 1918 overthrew the
monarchy and sued for peace. That coup was itself driven by the war s
unpopularity, which is war weariness doing exactly what this rule models: its
baseWeariness in 1918 works out near 19.
Estimated toll 400,000 military, 150,000 civilian and 15,000 in the revolution
= 565,000, which is 4.0% of a 1912 population near 14 million. Germany lost
4.2% in the real war, France 4.3%, Austria-Hungary 3.3%.
2,100 days of peace then carried 26.5% forward: 149,531 dead and 589 days,
split by population share.
NCN  26,397 mil + 36,000 civ + 43,767 carried = 106,164   modifier 0.85
CFR  18,312 mil + 33,750 civ + 30,362 carried =  82,424   modifier 1.05
The Franzonist Remnant is the wearest of the three: the smallest population,
fought by the other two at once, and no cause left to sell.
THE FUINAMESE CIVIL WAR, 18 Sithbruni 1924, 661 days. Ends 26 Sithbruni 1926,
77 days into play. CAF and KOF each claim all of the other s ground and fight
at 1.0; their satellites GAN, MWU and MNJ claim none of it, fight at 2.5 and
tire far faster than their patrons for it. No earlier war is carried.
CARRY RULE, for any war added later:
at peace  cumulativeDeaths *= 0.5 ^ (daysAtPeace / 1095)
daysAtWar        *= the same
Half a war is forgotten every three years. A country going to war again does
not start from nothing.
